integrate.idea: lab_server.py — a per-project JupyterLab manager cloned from preview_server (start_lab / stop_lab / list_labs / reap_orphans / ensure_lab), registry at .anchor/labs.json, loopback bind, OS port ≠ 8777, per-lab token, spawn through an `ANCHOR_LAB_CMD` seam so the STUB GATE + the 5 AM healthcheck run tests/fake_lab.py (a stdlib HTTP server answering /api/status and /lab/tree/*) and never a real jupyter; endpoints GET /api/rnd/labs?project_id= (SAFE projection: port/url/status, never token) + POST /api/rnd/lab_stop; a 'Lab' chip + stop control in the project window.

One open route for code: GET /notebook/<pid>?path=<rel>[&dir=<effort-rel>] (token-authed, 401 before substance, traversal-safe) that classifies the target — .ipynb → lab; .py/.R short (≤120 lines) or marked (`# %%` / `# notebook` in first lines) → convert once to sibling .ipynb → lab; else → editor — then ensure_lab (start, or restart when the probe fails) and 302 to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab/tree/<quoted rel>?token=<labtoken>`; the editor case returns a tiny page that fires `vscode://file/<abs>` (and the `code -r` fallback seam server-side) so the click always lands somewhere visible.

Pure classifier `code_open.open_kind(path) -> {kind: notebook|editor|lab, reason, lines, marker}` in stdlib (line count + first-lines marker scan + extension→kernel map python3/ir) exposed to the register/plan/files renderers so every row can print its mode chip ('notebook' / 'editor') without any spawn; the same function drives the route — one decision, rendered and executed identically. Also mirrored as `anchor.py rnd open-kind <pid> <path>` (inspection only).

Hand-written nbformat-4.5 writer: `to_notebook(src_path, kernel)` emits {nbformat:4, nbformat_minor:5, metadata.kernelspec{name,display_name,language}, cells:[one code cell with `id`, source as a list of lines, outputs:[], execution_count:null]} via json + temp/os.replace; never overwrites an existing .ipynb (returns it). Decision for the Judge: honor `# %%` markers by splitting into one cell per marker block (better notebook, same stdlib code) versus the North Star's literal one-cell — recommend split-on-marker, one-cell when unmarked.

Live-link Where cells: read_deliverables adds a `url` field when the cell's first http(s) URL has host ∈ {localhost, 127.0.0.1, tailnet short name, tailnet FQDN} (from `tailnet_names()` — cached `tailscale status --self --json` + `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES` override + hostname), any port, any path; delivRow gets a `url` branch: plain new-window anchor, NO Anchor token, textContent only; every other host stays the existing text branch. Also lets where_for accept an absolute URL verbatim so a campaign can register a JupyterLab/Shiny address directly (closing the 0110 launch-page workaround).

Client mapping in routeHref/delivRow (+ the plan-step and files-tile paths if they bypass delivRow): a `.ipynb`/`.py`/`.R` target in the in-effort backtick form or an `/artifact/<pid>?path=` route is rewritten to `/notebook/<pid>?path=<rel>&dir=<dir>` with the page token, opened `target=_blank`; the mode chip is appended from open_kind carried on the item — so the register, the plan outline and the files tile all inherit the behaviour from the same two functions.

Hygiene foresight (Oranges): JupyterLab writes `.ipynb_checkpoints/` into the project — add it to the project's git exclude via the existing project_bootstrap/worktrees exclude helper and to brownfield_scan/register ignore lists so checkpoints never surface as discovered docs or register rows; labs survive an NSSM restart because they live in their own process group, so boot-time reap_orphans must RE-ADOPT a still-alive, still-probing lab rather than only reconciling dead pids.

Sign-off wave: on a real project (this repo's planning docs) Playwright opens a `.ipynb` row → popup URL contains `/lab/tree/<rel>` and the JupyterLab document title equals the file name; a short `.py` row → sibling .ipynb appears exactly once (second click leaves bytes unchanged) and the popup lands in the lab; a long `.py` row → the row reads 'editor' and the fired href is `vscode://file/…`; a live-link row (`http://gwl-server…`) → an anchor without the Anchor token; screenshots kept under planning/…/signoff/; then `python tools/release.py` (v1.2.16) — the STUB GATE covers everything through fake_lab, the Playwright pass is the only real spawn.
